transitions.historical_text: FLIP: Select 1 monster on your opponent's side of the field and destroy it. When this card is sent directly from your hand to the Graveyard, return 1 Flip Effect Monster from your Graveyard to your hand.
transitions.modern_text: FLIP: Select 1 monster your opponent controls, and destroy it. When this card is sent directly from your hand to the Graveyard, select 1 Flip Effect Monster in your Graveyard, except this card, and return it to your hand.
transitions.summary: The hand-to-Graveyard retrieval gained a self-exclusion and an explicit selection step: AST-080 said only 'return 1 Flip Effect Monster from your Graveyard to your hand', naming no exception, so the Night Assailant just sent there is itself an eligible choice, while DT03-EN056 reads 'select 1 Flip Effect Monster in your Graveyard, except this card, and return it to your hand'. Project Ignis's pre-errata script implements the post-DT03 version - it targets and passes e:GetHandler() as the SelectTarget exception - so no upstream script reproduces the AST-era behaviour.

effective.basis: TCG release of OP19-EN016 (OTS Tournament Pack 19)

transitions.historical_text: FLIP: Target 1 monster your opponent controls; destroy that target.When this card is sent from the hand to the GY: Target 1 Flip monster in your GY, except this card; return that target to the hand.
transitions.modern_text: FLIP: Target 1 monster your opponent controls; destroy that target.If this card is sent from the hand to the GY: Target 1 Flip monster in your GY, except "Night Assailant"; add that target to your hand.
transitions.summary: Functional erratum: 'except this card' became 'except "Night Assailant"'. The pre-errata script excludes only the physical copy (SelectTarget exception e:GetHandler()), so a second copy of Night Assailant in the Graveyard is a legal retrieval; the modern filter adds 'not c:IsCode(id)', excluding every card with that name.

coverage.gap_reason: Project Ignis's only historical Night Assailant (cards-unofficial 16226796) implements the DT03-EN056 text; no upstream script implements the AST-080 text that both period snapshots need, so reproducing it needs a custom script and a reserved passcode

gap.behavioural_impact: In GOAT and Edison a Night Assailant sent from the hand to the Graveyard should be able to return itself (the era text names no exception); with the shipped pre-errata or modern script that choice is blocked, removing a recursion line the era decks had.

review.notes: The upstream code 16226796 is the card's own passcode +10, upstream's pre-errata convention, not an artwork variant. Its cdb text is exactly lineage v3 (SBCB-EN114, 2020-11-26), and v1 -> v2 (BP01-EN187, 2012-05-24, PSCT) -> v3 (GY wording) are cosmetic, so it implements the v1-v3 behaviour band. Remaining diff lines are cosmetic: the EFFECT_FLAG_CARD_TARGET property line is only reordered, function names differ (destg/desop vs target/operation), and the modern filter's added c:IsMonster() is redundant with TYPE_FLIP. The FLIP destruction half is unchanged across the whole lineage.
